page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARM64 architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz. It does not utilize hyperthreading, allocating exactly one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. No local NVMe or SSD storage is bundled with this instance type, and it does not include any integrated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring 192014.4 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 129079.05 in PassMark CPU extended instructions. Memory performance is highly competitive, with cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 13912.96 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 363.83 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2007.4. The instance excels in data processing tasks, achieving a top-tier bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 1131.71 GB/sec and a static web serving throughput of 198.56 GB/sec.

Given its high physical core count and strong memory bandwidth, the c9g.24xlarge is highly cost-efficient for highly parallelized, compute-bound workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for multi-threaded data compression, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
